question: Your developer productivity agent, built with the Claude Agent SDK, is configured with three MCP servers: a community Jira server, a team documentation server, and a database schema server. An engineer proposes a routing step that activates one server before each task, because he believes the agent can use tools from only one MCP server at a time. How do the tools from these three servers actually become available to the agent?

options.text: Each server's tools are discovered only when the agent first calls that server, so the tools appear one server at a time during the task.
options.reason: The guide states that discovery happens at connection time for all configured servers, not lazily at the first call to each server.

options.text: Tools from all three servers are discovered when the agent connects, and all of them are available to the agent at the same time.
options.reason: The guide states that tools from all configured MCP servers are discovered at connection time and are available to the agent simultaneously, so the routing step is unnecessary.

options.text: Only the tools of the first server in the configuration are loaded, and the other two servers stay inactive until that first server is disconnected.
options.reason: The guide states that tools from all configured servers are available simultaneously, so no server waits for another one to disconnect.

options.text: Tools from servers in .mcp.json are loaded at connection, while tools from servers in ~/.claude.json are loaded only after the agent requests them.
options.reason: The guide uses .mcp.json and ~/.claude.json only to separate shared team servers from personal servers; tools from all configured servers are discovered at connection time.
